kypExtensions.summary: The three-pass reading grammar for any distribution — CENTER (mean/median/mode ranked by outlier sensitivity: mean most affected, mode least, median rank-based with the even-n average-of-middle-two rule), SPREAD (SD scatters the values around their mean; SE scatters theoretical sample means around the true population mean; Variance = (SD)²; SE = σ/√n), SHAPE (Gaussian bell vs two humps vs one long tail) — feeding the printed routing rules: for normal distribution the mean is the best measure of central tendency, for skewed data the median is better than the mean, and bimodal data must be split into its two populations before summarizing.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the definitions and the two routing sentences as parallel rows; the three-pass protocol, the outlier-sensitivity ranking as a decision axis, and the split-the-bimodal instruction are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.what/core.why/core.keyIdea + mechanisms[0] shape-center-spread-map + blocks[4] the steps block + the registry visual's formula cards

kypExtensions.summary: The mechanism behind both printed skew orderings: every value enters the mean's sum, so the long tail drags the mean toward it ('mean falls closer to tail' prints for both skews) while the median only ranks and the mode sits at the peak — hence positive skew (tail right) gives mean > median > mode and negative skew (tail left) gives mean < median < mode, the inequality always pointing the same way as the tail; packaged with the 68-95-99.7 reading of the normal figure's below-axis braces (±1σ ≈ 68%, ±2σ ≈ 95%, ±3σ ≈ 99.7%) and the SE-vs-n square-root behavior (quadruple n, halve the SE).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the two orderings and the band labels but never states WHY the mean moves toward the tail, never states the tail/inequality direction-match rule, and never derives the √n pacing; the mechanism, the direction-match rule, and the corollary are KYP's.
kypExtensions.location: mechanisms[1] tail-drags-the-mean-map + blocks[3] the figure-decoder list + blocks[5] the compare block + mnemonics 2-4

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the printed page — 4 patterns (the long-right-tail ordering stem, the symmetric-bell best-measure stem, the SE-when-n-quadruples arithmetic stem, the P value definition stem), 4 traps (positive vs negative skew; SD vs SE; mean vs mode outlier sensitivity; H0 vs H1), 3 pivots (the best-measure router; the bimodal split-don't-average; the P value as a conditional computed assuming H0, against the probability-of-truth misreading), and 8 recall cards covering every printed row plus the figures.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the definitions only; the attack structure, the distractor options, and the classic P value misreading flag are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The mnemonic ledger: First Aid's OWN red-printed linkage — H0 ↔ 'zero' difference / H1 ↔ 'at least one' difference or association (the subscript 0 of H0, the subscript 1 of H1, and the words 'zero' and 'one' print in RED BOLD on book 265; texttrace + VLM census) — carried VERBATIM and ATTRIBUTED in the mnemonics array, the memory callout, the hypothesis table block, and the visual's H0/H1/P strip; plus THREE KYP originals, marked as such: 'THE MEAN CHASES THE TAIL' (both skew orderings via the dragging mechanism), '68–95–99.7 AT 1–2–3σ' (the normal bands), and 'QUADRUPLE n, HALVE THE SE' (the √n pacing of SE ↓ as n ↑).
kypExtensions.rationale: The red zero/one printing is the source's own emphasis (attributed, not counted as KYP's); no mnemonic prints anywhere on pdf 287 (pdfimages + the VLM census found none — no margin mnemonics); the three ALL-CAPS codes are KYP's design.
